item.title: Caribbean strikes: White House contradicts Trump amid scrutiny; defends Admiral behind follow up hit
item.description: The White House defended a second US military strike on a drug-smuggling vessel in September, stating the commander acted lawfully. This action has prompted bipartisan calls for investigations in Washington and a parallel inquiry in Venezuela into the deaths of its citizens. President Trump expressed reservations about the second strike but defended his defense secretary.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Streamer Subo assaulted live on stream by MMA fighter Shovkhal Churchaev
item.description: Gambling streamer Subo faced a violent assault live on air from MMA fighter Shovkhal Churchaev in Dubai. Subo's persistent taunts about Churchaev's career, including failed UFC attempts, provoked the fighter. The stream abruptly ended after Churchaev attacked Subo, leading to widespread debate on livestreaming ethics and the dangers of provocative content.

item.title: How exactly is Shivon Zilis “Indian”?
item.description: Shivon Zilis, Elon Musk's AI executive partner, is being celebrated in India due to her Punjabi heritage. While biologically half-Indian, Zilis identifies culturally as Canadian, having grown up and built her career in North America. India's pride stems from her elite global achievement and connection to Musk, highlighting how ancestry bridges cultures.

item.title: Why MeatCanyon was banned and unbanned on Twitch in November 2025
item.description: Popular creator MeatCanyon faced a brief, unexplained suspension on Twitch in late November 2025, leaving viewers puzzled. The ban, lasting just over a day, was quickly resolved without official explanation, fueling speculation about content violations and highlighting Twitch's opaque moderation system.

item.title: Nuclear war expert explains why Australia and New Zealand may be the last places left standing after WW3
item.description: In a deeply sourced analysis of nuclear war dynamics, investigative journalist Annie Jacobsen outlines how a global nuclear exchange could unfold within 72 minutes, killing billions and collapsing agriculture across most of Earth. Drawing on missile timing studies and nuclear-winter modelling by leading scientists, she argues that Australia and New Zealand may be among the only regions capable of sustaining food production in the aftermath.

item.title: Who is Jay Ma? Influencer goes viral after Louis Vuitton Cafe clip sparks talk about Jack Ma link
item.description: A viral video of influencer Jay Ma being hand-fed dessert at a Louis Vuitton Café sparked speculation he is Jack Ma's son. However, the scene appears staged, fitting Jay Ma's known 'rich kid' skits on social media. There is no evidence linking him to Jack Ma's family, suggesting the video is for online attention.

item.title: Mike Majlak fights rumor with strong clip as SteveWillDoIt is seen taking tequila from manager during Impaulsive podcast
item.description: Mike Majlak has addressed rumors about SteveWillDoIt's appearance on the Impaulsive podcast. A video shows Steve asking for alcohol, with his manager providing it. Majlak denies giving Steve alcohol, calling the claims untrue. Steve had previously called Majlak names online. The podcast episode ended abruptly after Steve's behavior. Steve was on the show to discuss his YouTube ban being lifted.

item.title: “This is so stupid”: Inside the controversy over Zentreya’s new model and the accusations fueling it
item.description: VTuber Zentreya faced backlash for her new "General Zentreya" model, with accusations of a "Nazi vibe" due to its military-inspired design. Zentreya vehemently denied any extremist connections, stating she is apolitical and against Nazism. Sponsor Tim Zheng criticized the accusations as "clout chasing" and needless drama.

item.title: Kash Patel's girlfriend Alexis Wilkins speaks up on H-1B row: 'We do not want this'
item.description: Alexis Wilkins, the partner of FBI Director Kash Patel, expressed her concerns regarding Congressman Subramanian Raja Krishnamoorthy's bill to double the H-1B visa cap. This development unfolds in a backdrop of conflicting views within the Trump administration about H-1B regulations, where the administration prioritizes American employment while recognizing the importance of foreign professionals in certain industries.

item.title: Man who beheaded Indin-origin motel owner in Texas won't face death penalty; prosecution goes soft on Cuban murderer
item.description: The chilling case of a beheading of an Indian-origin man in Texas, which initially sparked presidential interest, has evolved dramatically. Yordanis Cobos-Martinez, the accused, an undocumented immigrant from Cuba with a checkered past, will bypass death row and instead serve life in prison without the chance of parole.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Cory Booker weds Alexis Lewis: Decoding the homosexuality rumours that have persisted for long
item.description: Senator Cory Booker's recent marriage to Alexis Lewis has reignited long-standing, baseless rumors about his sexuality. These whispers, circulating for over two decades, stemmed from his articulate nature and initial privacy regarding his orientation. Despite his marriage, the internet's tendency to cling to speculation highlights societal discomfort with complexity and stereotypes surrounding masculinity and public figures.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Putin is coming to India in December 2025: Which other Russian presidents visited India, including Putin’s past trips
item.description: President Vladimir Putin's upcoming December 2025 visit to India for the 23rd Annual Summit underscores the enduring Special and Privileged Strategic Partnership. This meeting, following a period of limited high-level interactions, aims to bolster defense, space, energy, and trade cooperation. Past visits by Putin, Medvedev, and Yeltsin have cemented this robust, trust-based relationship.
